einzeiler: Understanding the Wall of Awful and emotional barriers with Brendan Mahan
kurzfassung: Brendan Mahan discusses his concept of the Wall of Awful, a metaphorical emotional barrier built from repeated failures that makes everyday tasks feel impossible. The conversation explores the distinction between this barrier, boundaries, and burnout, as well as strategies like climbing and adding doors to overcome them. They also examine the role of emotions such as anxiety and anger in motivation and the importance of self-compassion.
stichpunkte: The Wall of Awful is an emotional barrier built from real or imagined failures that hinders task initiation.
Bricks in the wall are held together by anxiety, along with negative emotions like guilt, shame, and frustration.
Smashing through the wall using anxiety or anger works temporarily but frequently leads directly to burnout.
Distinguishing between walls of awful, preferences, and personal boundaries helps clarify task avoidance.
A redesigned emotion wheel in the book maps feelings by comfort and activation levels to guide coping strategies.
Recognizing and naming emotional states shifts processing from the limbic system to the prefrontal cortex.
The book's structure covers foundations, problem-solving, strategies for getting past the wall, systems, and planning.
Relapse and setbacks are normal parts of behavioral change, requiring patience and sustained hope.

clips.hook: The emotional impact of repeated failure
clips.text: The model explains how emotional responses accumulate following repeated missteps, affecting neurodivergent individuals more frequently due to higher failure rates.

clips.hook: Anxiety is the only fuel that leaves you with more
clips.text: Relying on stress and worry as a motivational tool uniquely generates an increased surplus of that exact negative feeling once finished.

clips.hook: Burnout is like trying to wade through deep mud
clips.text: Unlike facing a single barrier, chronic exhaustion feels like constant slogging that leaves a heavy residue weighing down future efforts long afterward.

clips.hook: Shifting from emotional panic to logical problem-solving
clips.text: Identifying and verbalizing specific feelings activates the brain's logical regions, pulling a person away from pure stress and anxiety.
The authors intentionally designed the entire book to ensure optimism remains present throughout challenging discussions on difficult psychological obstacles.

beschreibung:
Hey Team!
This week I got a chance to catch up with my good friend Brendan Mahan and talk with him about his upcoming book, Overcoming the Wall of Awful. Brendan is one of the first people I got to know in the ADHD space and I feel lucky to have done so because for one he's just an awesome guy, but also because his approach to ADHD has always just felt so real and coming from a place of lived experience. Brendan is the host of the ADHD Essentials Podcast, a board member of the Men's ADHD Support Group and the Director of Professional Resources for Calmer Con: Boston - and also one of the few people I know who gets me to sit down and listen because it's always worth hearing what he has to say.
Today on the show we're going to be talking about a book that Brendan spent a decade being asked to write. After finding his co-writer, Alex Hughes Capell, Brendan brought us the book we've been waiting for. So for those of you who are unfamiliar, the Wall of Awful is a concept that Brendan developed to explain the metaphorical emotional barrier that builds up over time and makes starting basic, everyday tasks feel nearly impossible. Or, in simpler terms, the barrier that keeps us from starting what often feels like a simple task, such as doing the dishes or starting our homework.
In our conversation, we discuss the ways that we build up these walls and also ways that we can work on getting past these walls (and what doesn't work). We also dive into the distinction between burnout and the wall and get into the nitty-gritty of the Wall of Awful.
If you'd like to follow along on the show notes page you can find that at HackingYourADHD.com/308
YouTube: https://tinyurl.com/y835cnrk
Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/HackingYourADHD
This Episode's Top Tips
Worth restating here, the Wall of Awful is a metaphorical emotional barrier that builds up over time and makes starting basic, everyday tasks feel nearly impossible. And it's important to acknowledge that we can build this wall from both real and perceived failure.
While smashing through our walls by activating through anger or anxiety often works, it's not always enough to get us completely through the wall. So while it may get us started it doesn't always get us to the finish line. As well, smashing often comes with a cost in terms of relationships, both to ourselves and to others who are hurt in the process of smashing through the wall.
It's important that we're able to distinguish our walls from preferences and boundaries. While our walls are built out of the emotional response to failure, preferences aren't built out of failure. It may be something we don't like doing but we can get past it without reaching for our wall tools. And boundaries are choices that we make not out of our sense of failure but instead our sense of who we are.
